sources.title: MIVUBI Teleport Dimension Transfer and Spawn Safety Policy v1

facts.subject: teleport destination
facts.statement: Every gameplay teleport destination must declare dimension, position, orientation policy, collision policy, chunk-readiness policy, arena ownership, and expected post-teleport state. Raw coordinates alone are insufficient.

facts.subject: teleport ownership
facts.statement: A player/entity may have at most one accepted critical teleport owner per transition purpose/generation. Competing lobby, respawn, cutscene, arena-start, recovery, and knockback-return teleports must arbitrate ownership rather than overwrite each other.

facts.subject: deferred teleport
facts.statement: Deferred teleport work must capture player/entity identity, connection/entity validity, arenaGeneration, participation/life generation where relevant, teleportGeneration, and destination contract version; all are revalidated immediately before teleport.

facts.subject: cross-dimension transfer
facts.statement: For cross-dimension gameplay transfer, destination dimension and target area must be resolved and made ready before moving the player. World mutation/structure setup that defines the destination must VERIFY before teleport begins.

facts.subject: collision-sensitive teleport
facts.statement: When placement safety matters, use a collision-aware teleport path such as tryTeleport/checkForBlocks or an equivalent explicit occupancy validation, and treat failure as a recoverable routing result rather than silently forcing success.

facts.subject: teleport commit
facts.statement: A critical teleport is committed only after verifying the entity/player remains valid and its current dimension/location satisfy the destination contract within tolerance. API call completion alone is APPLY evidence.

facts.subject: respawn routing
facts.statement: Respawn-point authority and immediate teleport authority must be tracked separately. Setting a spawn point must not be used as proof that the player has already moved, and teleporting a player must not silently redefine future respawn policy unless explicitly intended.

facts.subject: spawn safety volume
facts.statement: Destination safety should validate the entity/player occupancy volume and nearby support/fall hazards where gameplay requires it, not merely inspect a single destination block coordinate.

facts.subject: teleport recovery
facts.statement: Critical player routing should define an ordered fallback chain such as exact target, validated nearby safe point, arena fallback, and lobby/safe recovery point. Failed primary teleport must not leave gameplay state committed as if transfer succeeded.

facts.subject: state and spatial ordering
facts.statement: For transitions where location defines membership/phase, do not commit target gameplay state before the destination transfer is verified unless the transition protocol explicitly supports compensating rollback. Prevent state saying ARENA_ACTIVE while the player remains in lobby.

facts.subject: multi-player arena transfer
facts.statement: When multiple players must enter an arena together, define a transfer barrier: track each participant result, handle individual failures, and commit group start only when the game mode's required transfer quorum is satisfied.
